The WanderWise Verified Visa Dataset

A continuously re-verified dataset of tourist visa requirements covering up to 199 origin passports × 199 destination countries, each entry tagged with an official government source URL and a confidence tier. Free to use under CC-BY 4.0 — just link back when you cite us.

15,244 verified passport→destination pairs
69 residence-permit exemptions (hand-compiled)
199 × 199 full matrix target

What's in the dataset

verified-visas.json

Download JSON →

Tier-2 dataset. Every entry has a status (vf, voa, ev, eta, vr, unknown), max-stay days, the official government source URL, a confidence tier (high / medium / low / unknown), and a verification date.

{
  "data": {
    "India": {
      "Japan": {
        "passport": "India",
        "destination": "Japan",
        "status": "vr",
        "days": null,
        "source": "https://www.mofa.go.jp/...",
        "notes": "Tourist visa required; apply at the Embassy of Japan.",
        "confidence": "high",
        "verified_at": "2026-06-07"
      }
    }
  }
}

residence-permits.json

Download JSON →

Tier-1 dataset. Hand-compiled visa-exemption rules for 7 residence permit types (UAE residence, US Green Card, Schengen residence, UK BRP, Canada PR, valid US visa, valid Schengen visa). Each entry carries a source URL to the issuing government page.

visa-matrix.json

Download JSON →

Tier-3 baseline from the open-source Passport Index Dataset — community-maintained, no per-entry sources. Use only when no verified entry exists.

countries.json

Download JSON →

Canonical country-name list (199 entries) used as keys across all the datasets above.

How to use it

The dataset is plain JSON — fetch from a browser, script, or LLM agent. Examples:

curl https://wanderwise.techtools365.com/data/verified-visas.json | jq '.data.India.Japan'

# Python
import requests
data = requests.get("https://wanderwise.techtools365.com/data/verified-visas.json").json()
print(data["data"]["India"]["Japan"]["status"])  # "vr"

For agent / LLM use: see /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt — both list the data files and explain how to interpret the confidence tiers.
